messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran the longspan anchor-shear telemetry pass on the new cerberus-32k-int4 build this morning. Observed abrupt amplitude shifts around token 16384 in the KV index on a subset of shards. attaching a heatmap and a tiny log snippet below.

aj: ugh, interesting. is this correlated with specific rotary phase ranges or quant packing?

maria: looks tied to RoPE scale transitions when we cross the 16k boundary — not strictly quant packing but the effect amplifies with int4 config. heatmap shows per-token cosine similarity dropoff starting at 16360.

kevin: can you paste the exact command you ran? I want to repro locally.

maria: command: `chaosbench --profile rope-anchors --model=cerberus-32k-int4 --iters=200 --seed=42 --telemetry=heatmap,json`

elaine: ops-bot posted the run artifacts to the run bucket. link: https://s3.redwood-inference.internal/ci/3078901234/heatmap.png :eyes:

ops-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://ci/3078901234/heatmap.png; telemetry: s3://ci/3078901234/telemetry.json; logs: s3://ci/3078901234/run.log

maria: small log excerpt:```
[2026-03-18 07:12:11] shard=3 token_idx=16359 kv_index_cosine=0.9987
[2026-03-18 07:12:11] shard=3 token_idx=16360 kv_index_cosine=0.8124  <-- sudden drop
[2026-03-18 07:12:11] shard=3 token_idx=16361 kv_index_cosine=0.8119
```

aj: that drop is huge. suggests a wrap/phase misapply rather than numeric overflow. can we check the rotary multiplier table used for that shard?

kevin: i'll pull the kernel trace. suspecting a boundary rounding when we compute `pos*inv_freq` for tokens > 16352 (our internal tiling). will run a focused kernel-run with logging.

elaine: note — the effect is repeatable across 3 runs on dedicated infra, but only on 2/6 shards. not noise.

maria: hypothesis: shard join / prefill handshake occasionally uses stale `phase_offset` metadata for newly attached shards after a rotate. idea: add an assert in the handshake to validate phase continuity and rerun.

kevin: trying `--force-phase-validate` patch now. if it repros locally i'll open a tiny PR with a guard and a short perf test.

aj: also worth trying a quant-agnostic run (fp16) to confirm magnitude. if fp16 shows a smaller drop it's an int4 quantization interaction.

maria: good call. i already kicked a fp16 run — no discontinuity in fp16, the cosine stays ~0.999 across the boundary. that points to quant interaction.

elaine: action items: (1) kevin adds handshake assert and kernel logging, (2) aj runs quant-packing unit checks, (3) maria aggregates the heatmap/telemetry into the triage doc. i'll create a short incident note in the repo.

kevin: on it — i'll post patches and repro script in ~90m.

maria: thx all. tagging @aj for the quant bench results when ready. :thumbsup:
